title: Project Overview
description: Start with README.md to understand what skills-ui is: a self-contained Bun executable that wraps the stock skills CLI across an OpenTUI terminal app, a local web dashboard, a headless loopback HTTP API, and a hosted GitHub Pages frontend. Pair it with CONTEXT.md, the domain glossary that pins shared terminology across both interfaces, including layout panels, Skill Provenance (locked, linked, local), Post-Mutation Hooks, and the Health Pill. Together, these two documents frame the architectural boundaries and vocabulary you will see throughout the codebase.

title: CLI Entry Point
description: Moving from documentation into executable code, src/main.ts is the sole CLI entry point that parses --port and routes execution to --version, --selftest, headless serve, interactive --web, or the default OpenTUI application. When invoked with subcommands like add, update, or remove, src/core/seed.ts parses those arguments into a structured UiSeed so whichever UI launches can pre-populate the matching tab and selections. Meanwhile, src/core/version.ts supplies the single APP_VERSION constant by reading the compile-time __APP_VERSION__ define in release binaries and falling back to package.json during local development.

title: Shared Core Runtime Primitives
description: Before examining specific UIs or services, look at the shared runtime primitives that keep the TUI and WebUI visually and behaviorally consistent. prefs.ts persists theme, sound, reduced-motion, port, and list-width settings in ~/.config/skills-ui/prefs.json, while theme.ts defines Catppuccin Mocha and Latte palettes with WCAG AA contrast tokens for both terminal ANSI output and CSS. filter.ts defines the single skillMatches predicate shared verbatim across TUI and browser filtering, and disk-index.ts stores atomic stale-while-revalidate caches under ~/.cache/skills-ui so the TUI can paint hundreds of skills instantly on launch.
languageLesson: Writing pure, template-literal-safe TypeScript in src/core/filter.ts allows the web renderer to inline the transpiled function directly into the browser script, guaranteeing identical filtering semantics across Bun and browser runtimes without a separate client bundler.

title: Subprocess Boundary & Sanitization
description: Because skills-ui intentionally has no build-time dependency on the upstream skills package, every CLI invocation crosses a hardened subprocess boundary. skills-client.ts resolves the skills executable at runtime (SKILLS_UI_SKILLS_BIN then PATH), filters child environment variables through allowlists and denylists, and enforces command timeouts, while spawn-queue.ts serializes child processes through a bounded FIFO semaphore that fails fast with SkillsBusyError under request storms. Every external string coming back across that boundary is scrubbed by sanitize.ts against CWE-150 terminal escape injection, and src/core/index.ts exposes the clean barrel API consumed by upper layers.
languageLesson: A bounded async FIFO semaphore (spawn-queue.ts) queues Promise resolvers in JavaScript's single-threaded event loop to cap concurrent child processes without busy-waiting, while barrel files (src/core/index.ts) use explicit re-exports to define a clear module facade.

title: Core Skill Domain Services
description: Building on the subprocess boundary from Step 4, the domain services implement skill discovery and lifecycle mutations against the shared interfaces in types.ts. installed.ts wraps skills ls --json and combines symlink inspection with locks.ts's read-only lockfile parser (skills-lock.json and global XDG .skill-lock.json) to classify each skill's provenance as locked, linked, or local while surfacing per-entry diagnostics. install.ts wraps skills add --yes --json with ingress sanitization, and remove.ts verifies deletions by diffing before-and-after skill lists via injectable callbacks so the HTTP API can reuse its warm cache.

title: Search, Updates & Hooks
description: Beyond wrapping the skills CLI, several domain services read local files or talk to external registries directly to keep hot paths fast and extensible. search.ts queries the public skills.sh registry with in-flight request deduplication and fuzzy fallback strategies, while updates-check.ts compares locked GitHub folder SHAs from Step 5's lock reader against the GitHub Trees API with strict completeness checks and null-prototype result maps. skill-doc.ts reads and strips YAML frontmatter from SKILL.md files on disk with zero subprocesses, and hooks.ts executes user-configured SKILLS_UI_POST_MUTATION_HOOK and TTL-cached SKILLS_UI_HEALTH_CMD commands in sanitized environments.

title: Loopback HTTP API & Auth
description: When launched with serve or --web from Step 2, src/core/api.ts starts a Bun.serve loopback server that exposes all domain services from Steps 5 and 6 over JSON endpoints. To shield users from slow upstream skills ls scans, the server maintains per-scope list caches, coalesces concurrent reads, enforces request body limits and token-bucket rate limits, and serves zero-spawn detail lookups by exact path. hosted-auth.ts guards the browser-to-loopback boundary for both local and hosted GitHub Pages clients with persisted constant-time bearer tokens, DNS-rebinding Host checks, cross-site Fetch Metadata rejection, and strict CORS preflight handling.
languageLesson: Binding to 127.0.0.1 alone does not protect a local HTTP API from malicious browser tabs: validating Host/Origin headers blocks DNS rebinding, checking Sec-Fetch-Site rejects cross-site requests, and constant-time token comparison prevents timing leaks.

title: OpenTUI State & Views
description: When launched in default terminal mode, skills-ui runs an OpenTUI React application structured around an Elm-style separation of pure state, imperative runtime effects, and declarative rendering. model.ts defines the renderer-agnostic TuiModel, its Action union, immutable reducers, and scope-isolated filtering and sorting projections reusing Step 3's skillMatches predicate. app.ts orchestrates core services, instant SWR hydration from disk-index.ts, debounced search, crash guards, and the keyboard contract, while Views.tsx subscribes to the store via useSyncExternalStore to paint the split-pane tabs, overlays, and health strip.
languageLesson: TypeScript discriminated unions (Action in model.ts) let the compiler check state transitions exhaustively, while React's useSyncExternalStore safely bridges an external imperative store into declarative components without concurrent tearing.

title: TUI Media, 3D & Selftest
description: Complementing the core TUI views from Step 8, these modules add procedural media, 3D visualization, and deterministic headless verification without bundling static image or audio files into the executable. art.ts synthesizes Catppuccin RGBA splash gradients and deterministic source identicons in memory, audio.ts generates preference-gated 44.1 kHz PCM feedback tones, and three-scene.ts builds a 3D Fibonacci-sphere skills graph via @opentui/three. Finally, spike.ts defines the tree-sitter markdown selftest screen invoked by --selftest, and renderer-ready.ts polls in-memory frames deterministically so smoke checks never rely on brittle sleeps.

title: Single-File Web Dashboard UI
description: The web frontend mirrors the TUI's split-pane workflow in a single standalone HTML document served locally by Step 7's API or exported to GitHub Pages for zero-install hosted use. page.ts assembles the Catppuccin CSS from styles.ts together with three modular browser JavaScript fragments: core.ts for sessionStorage-backed bearer auth, WebAudio cues, and hosted connection probing; installed.ts for keyed DOM-reusing row reconciliation, shared filter parity, and escape-first SKILL.md markdown rendering; and search-and-boot.ts for registry search, batch install queues, and startup bootstrapping. For defense-in-depth, page.ts computes SHA-256 hashes of every emitted script block to serve a strict Content-Security-Policy without script unsafe-inline.

title: Build, Release & Verified Install
description: Turning the TypeScript codebase into a distributable binary starts in package.json, which declares Bun >=1.4 dependencies and developer scripts for testing, building, and exporting the hosted page. scripts/build.ts cross-compiles src/main.ts into four standalone darwin and linux executables with __APP_VERSION__ baked in, macOS JIT codesigning, and a SHA-256 checksums manifest, which scripts/verify-build-targets.ts audits for target architecture and digest accuracy. End users consume those artifacts through scripts/install.sh, a POSIX shell installer that verifies SHA-256 checksums against tag-committed manifests and swaps binaries atomically, following the full release checklist documented in docs/release.md.

title: Testing, Performance Budgets & CI
description: To verify every layer hermetically without mutating real user skills or hitting live registries, the test architecture centers on tests/fixtures/skills-shim.mjs, an executable CLI stand-in with persistent state files, failure injection, and JSONL spawn logging. Security and resilience invariants (timing-safe auth, spawn-queue 503 overflow, body caps, and cross-site fetch rejection) are pinned in tests/serve-hardening.test.ts, while scripts/perf/budget.ts benchmarks API caching, search deduplication, and Playwright DOM row identity against ratified budgets. Real-terminal behavior is verified end-to-end inside a Python pyte pseudoterminal by scripts/pty-smoke/smoke.py, and .github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml automates pull-request reviews in GitHub Actions.
languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows define event triggers (on: pull_request), least-privilege permissions, and sequential job steps in YAML to run automated PR review gates alongside hermetic local shims and real-PTY smoke harnesses.
